name: decide
description: From a still-muddy want to a defensible choice: outcome shaping, wide option generation, option development to comparable depth, honest recommendations, design exploration to an approved design, one-invocation autonomous deliberation, and scope cutting under a binding constraint

interface.shortDescription: Shape a want, widen the field, develop the options, and choose honestly
interface.longDescription: Seven skills covering one arc from a still-muddy want to a defensible choice. outcome-shaping helps the user build a want they can stand behind through an interview-style shaping conversation, typed by why they cannot say it yet and load-tested with priced trades. ideate widens a clear-enough prompt into a deliberately un-ranked field of genuinely different options and stops before any ranking. option-shaping develops a fixed field of sketch-level options to comparable resolution without ranking or choosing. making-recommendations chooses among serious, comparable options like an honest advisor: filters, dominance, genuine trades compared in words, the runner-up's strongest case, and the priced values question when the ranking turns on it. design-exploration shapes a clear-enough outcome into compared approaches and an approved design before any implementation lane takes over. deliberate runs Generate, Prune, Shape, Recommend, and Contest autonomously in one explicit invocation and returns a close plus a re-run capsule. scope-cut partitions an already-shaped scope into keep, defer, and cut under a binding constraint, preserving every removed item with a re-entry condition.
defaultPrompt: Help me work out what I actually want here before we choose a next move
Brainstorm a wide field of genuinely different options for this
Develop these fixed options to comparable depth without ranking them
Recommend between these options and give me the case against your pick
Explore the design approaches for this and settle one before we implement
Use $deliberate to run a complete autonomous deliberation on this decision frame
This scope is too big for the deadline; cut it to a defensible slice
